name: Gideon’s ephod
charge: Making an ephod of the golden earrings of the spoil, and putting it in Ophrah; all Israel going a whoring after it
summary: The men of Israel asked Gideon to rule over them, and his son and grandson after him, for saving them from Midian, and he refused: the Lord would rule over them. Then he asked every man for the earrings from his plunder, because the enemy were Ishmaelites and wore gold earrings, and made an ephod of seventeen hundred shekels of gold and set it up in his city. All Israel went after it there in spiritual whoredom, and it became a snare to Gideon and to his house. As soon as he was dead the people went after the Baals again and made Baal-berith their god.
offenseFull: The men of Israel asked Gideon to rule over them, he and his son and his grandson, because he had saved them from Midian (Judges 8:22-27). Israel has always needed a leader, because we are lost sheep and wander off the path without somebody to guide us in the way we must go. Gideon refused the throne for himself and his son, because the Lord was their ruler. He knew that if thrones were set up in Israel the people would put their trust and their faith in the king instead of in the Most High. Those were right words, and the man who spoke them had already torn down his father’s altar of Baal and cut down the grove beside it (Judges 6:25-27). The test did not end when he refused the crown.

He made one request: that every man give him the earrings from his plunder, since the enemy, being Ishmaelites, wore gold earrings. They gave gladly, spreading a garment and throwing the earrings on it, and the gold weighed seventeen hundred shekels, not counting the ornaments, pendants and purple garments of the Midianite kings and the chains from their camels’ necks. Gideon made an ephod of it and set it up in his city of Ophrah, and all Israel went after it there in spiritual whoredom, and it became a snare to Gideon and to his house. Paul names the love of money as the root of evil (1 Timothy 6:10); the gold Gideon gathered turned into the very snare that trapped his own house.
judgmentFull: The judgment is already in the word the record chooses: a snare. No sentence is passed on Gideon in the chapter, and none needed to be written; the man who had pulled down one idol furnished the people with another object to go after, and his own house was caught in it. Midian stayed subdued and the land was quiet forty years in Gideon’s days; he fathered seventy sons, for he had many wives, and his concubine in Shechem also bore him a son he named Abimelech, and Gideon the son of Joash died at a good old age (Judges 8:28-35).

As soon as Gideon was dead, the children of Israel turned again to spiritual whoredom after the Baals and made Baal-berith their god (Judges 8:33-35). Baal means lord and berith means covenant, so the god they set up was the lord of the covenant, a counterfeit put over the people in place of the One who had just delivered them. They forgot the Lord their God who had rescued them from all the enemies around them, and showed no kindness to the house of Jerubbaal, that is Gideon, for all the good he had done Israel. The same cycle turned again the moment the judge was gone. That is the whole lesson of the book: our deliverance is never our own hand, and our downfall is always our own forgetting. The son born of the concubine in Shechem, and the silver out of the house of Baal-berith, are the next case.

text.text: Then the men of Israel said unto Gideon, Rule thou over us, both thou, and thy son, and thy son’s son also: for thou hast delivered us from the hand of Midian.
And Gideon said unto them, I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you: the Lord shall rule over you.
And Gideon said unto them, I would desire a request of you, that ye would give me every man the earrings of his prey. (For they had golden earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.)
And they answered, We will willingly give them. And they spread a garment, and did cast therein every man the earrings of his prey.

And the weight of the golden earrings that he requested was a thousand and seven hundred shekels of gold; beside ornaments, and collars, and purple raiment that was on the kings of Midian, and beside the chains that were about their camels’ necks.
And Gideon made an ephod thereof, and put it in his city, even in Ophrah: and all Israel went thither a whoring after it: which thing became a snare unto Gideon, and to his house.

And it came to pass the same night, that the Lord said unto him, Take thy father’s young bullock, even the second bullock of seven years old, and throw down the altar of Baal that thy father hath, and cut down the grove that is by it:

And build an altar unto the Lord thy God upon the top of this rock, in the ordered place, and take the second bullock, and offer a burnt sacrifice with the wood of the grove which thou shalt cut down.

Then Gideon took ten men of his servants, and did as the Lord had said unto him: and so it was, because he feared his father’s household, and the men of the city, that he could not do it by day, that he did it by night.
For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
Thus was Midian subdued before the children of Israel, so that they lifted up their heads no more. And the country was in quietness forty years in the days of Gideon.
And Jerubbaal the son of Joash went and dwelt in his own house.
And Gideon had threescore and ten sons of his body begotten: for he had many wives.
And his concubine that was in Shechem, she also bare him a son, whose name he called Abimelech.
And Gideon the son of Joash died in a good old age, and was buried in the sepulchre of Joash his father, in Ophrah of the Abi–ezrites.
And it came to pass, as soon as Gideon was dead, that the children of Israel turned again, and went a whoring after Baalim, and made Baal–berith their god.
And the children of Israel remembered not the Lord their God, who had delivered them out of the hands of all their enemies on every side:
Neither shewed they kindness to the house of Jerubbaal, namely, Gideon, according to all the goodness which he had shewed unto Israel.
